method: Each normative rule of CONTRACT.md is listed with the tests that exercise it: upstream (federation-port's own suite at the pinned revision, named by test id or full title), REMORA (component and acceptance tests, file and title), and probes (integrations/federation-port/contract-probes, run against the unmodified runtime). A rule with no test before this map got one or more probes. Coverage was established by reading each test against the rule, not by matching reason codes alone. The probe file's last test checks that every upstream and probe name here exists; tests/test_federation_port_contract_coverage.py checks the REMORA names.

statuses.covered: exercised by an upstream or REMORA test before this map
statuses.probed: not exercised before; one or more contract probes now do
statuses.partly_covered: some forms exercised before; probes cover the rest
statuses.stated_limit: the contract states the limit itself; a test would only restate it

clauses.rule: workflow and tool, describe() against the pin, args schema, approval id, approval not consumed, required claims; anything else refuses
optional claims are recorded with their status, or unevaluated
the admission deadline is the earliest valid_until of a component supplying a required claim; optional components cannot shorten it
approval required and no deadline: admission_deadline_missing
the clock is read after the write lock is held; waiting counts against the deadline
a second consumer of an approval, in this or another process, gets approval_already_consumed
a process that dies before the admission transaction commits has consumed nothing
a transport error after the request may have been sent is unknown, never failed
dispatch is claimed under a lease, so concurrent retries do not double-dispatch; a crashed worker's lease expires
a confirmed operation replays its result without dispatch
a retry runs only under the stored workflow, tenant, action, approval, submitted evidence and execution context

a refused retry does not change the stored operation
past the deadline, unknown (or an expired lease) is retried with the same key; a retriable failure is closed
manifest, artifact, version, privileges, destinations, secrets, createAdapter, role method and describe() are checked at load
provenance carries digests and identifiers: no action arguments, evidence bytes or secrets
one usage row per component per logical operation; calls counts invocations including retries

clauses.note: Both REMORA components request no privilege, secret or destination. That is a declaration, not confinement; the contract says so.

clauses.rule: no revocation, trusted time, key rotation or tenant authentication; clock skew between workers is not handled
clauses.note: CP-F1 shows one concrete consequence of unhandled clock skew.

findings.observed: When a second worker claims attempt 2 after attempt 1's lease expired, and attempt 1 then returns provider_confirmed, finishAttempt records that outcome on the attempt row but not on the operation, because the operation's attempt counter has moved on. If attempt 2 ended failed and retriable (its own request never arrived), the operation stays failed, the first worker's caller is told failed, and after the deadline the operation is closed with approval_expired_before_retry. The provider performed the refund.
findings.conditions: Attempt 1 must still be running when another worker sees its lease as expired. In one process the execute timeout ends attempt 1 first, so this takes clock skew between workers (section 10 says it is not handled) or a stalled event loop.
findings.consequence: The operation's terminal state and the effect disagree, and the closing rule's reason (a retry would be a first side effect after expiry) is false for this operation. No second effect: the idempotency key holds.
findings.suggested_change: Treat provider_confirmed from any attempt as final for the operation, as the comment on finishAttempt already intends for a confirmation recorded first.

findings.observed: An attempt that ends unknown without having sent anything (here a throw before the request is written) is retried after valid_until under the after-deadline rule. The provider's first request arrives an hour after the deadline, and the operation is confirmed.
findings.conditions: Any executor outcome of unknown on attempt 1, including the runtime's mapping of a thrown error or a timeout.
findings.consequence: Section 5.5 calls valid_until the last instant the claims may be acted on. The deadline bounds admission and retriable failures, not the first contact with the provider. Executors that can tell "not sent" from "sent, no answer" should report failed and retriable for the first.
findings.suggested_change: Either state in section 5.5 that the deadline bounds admission, or record in provenance when an attempt's first provider contact falls after the deadline.

findings.observed: A claim's reason string is stored and returned verbatim and without a length bound. An adapter that puts the action arguments, evidence or a secret into a reason puts them into provenance; a 100 kB reason is accepted.
findings.conditions: An adapter that writes payload data into reason text, by mistake or otherwise. Executor reasons and thrown error messages are cut to 120 characters but not filtered.
findings.consequence: Section 9's no-arguments rule holds for what the runtime writes, and for adapter text only by each adapter's discipline.
findings.suggested_change: Bound claim reasons to a short code form in normalizeCheckOutput, or state the obligation on adapters in section 9.

findings.observed: Attempt 1 reaches the provider and its response is lost, so the operation is unknown. The retry cannot reach the provider and honestly reports failed and retriable; the operation takes that outcome. Past the deadline the retriable failure is closed with approval_expired_before_retry. The operation ends failed, not retriable, while the provider performed the refund.
findings.conditions: One worker, no clock skew, no crash: a lost response followed by a provider outage before the deadline. Found by the TLA+ model formal/tla/LeaseRetry.tla (configuration pinned_outage) before the probe was written.
findings.consequence: The closing rule of section 7 rests on failed-and-retriable meaning that no side effect happened, but a later attempt's failure says nothing about an earlier attempt that may have reached the provider. CP-F1 is the same fault reached through clock skew.
findings.suggested_change: Uncertainty sticky: a failed outcome, retriable or not, sets the operation to failed only if every earlier attempt reported a retriable failure; otherwise the operation stays unknown and is retried with the same key. The TLA+ model holds under this rule with outages, crashes and clock skew; making a confirmation final alone does not. The model has no non-retriable failure; the upstream test E4 covers that case in the runtime.
